evals.prompt: Acme finance wants this in Excel: exports/northwind-invoices.csv. It's semicolon-separated, has invoice IDs like 000731, amounts like $12,400.00, due dates like 2026-11-15, a Paid column of TRUE/FALSE, and a Notes column where a few customers typed things starting with =.
assertions: Runs md_to_xlsx.py on the CSV and writes a .xlsx
Leaves --formulas off and explains that cells starting with = from an export are kept as text because of formula injection
Reports that invoice IDs with leading zeros stay text so 000731 keeps its zeros
Reports the per-sheet summary (rows, columns, numbers, dates, booleans, text) and checks the amounts became numbers
Does not change, round or fill in any value from the CSV
Reopens or previews the workbook to confirm it opens, rather than relying on exit code 0

evals.prompt: Turn the tables in reports/q3-ops-review.md into a spreadsheet for Northwind's ops leads. There are four tables; two are under '## Results' and one has the heading '### Incidents by severity: P1 / P2 / P3 (Jul–Sep, all regions)'.
assertions: Gives each table its own short heading before converting, so no sheet is named 'Results (2)' or cut off by the script
The incidents sheet name is 31 characters or fewer with no / or : in it
Lists every sheet with its name, rows and columns in the reply
Reports any WARN lines (renames, padded rows) with what was done about them
Does not invent rows, totals or values that are not in the Markdown
